                  https://doi.org/10.3390/nu11030698
                  
                .")]. The Mediterranean diet is characterized by a substantial consumption of vegetables, legumes, fruits, nuts, cereals, and olive oil, with a moderate intake of wine, meat, fish, eggs, and dairy products, and a low intake of red meat, processed foods, and sugary drinks [[41](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1186/s12889-024-17880-9#ref-CR41 "deKoning L, Anand SS. Adherence to a Mediterranean diet and survival in a Greek population., Trichopoulou A, Costacou T, Bamia C, Trichopoulos D. N Engl J Med. 2003; 348: 2599– 608. Vascular medicine (London, England). 2004;9(2):145-6; 
                  https://doi.org/10.1191/1358863x04vm552xx
                  
                ."), [42](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1186/s12889-024-17880-9#ref-CR42 "Rubini A, Vilaplana-Prieto C, Flor-Alemany M, Yeguas-Rosa L, Hernandez-Gonzalez M, Felix-Garcia FJ, et al. Assessment of the cost of the Mediterranean Diet in a low-income region: adherence and relationship with available incomes. BMC Public Health. 2022;22(1). 
                  https://doi.org/10.1186/s12889-021-12433-w
                  
                .")].

To our knowledge, there has been limited exploration of the relationship between healthy dietary patterns and SWB, with the majority of the studies in the literature solely focused on the Mediterranean diet and limited by cross-sectional study design [[39](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1186/s12889-024-17880-9#ref-CR39 "Godoy-Izquierdo D, Ogallar A, Lara R, Rodriguez-Tadeo A, Arbinaga F. Association of a Mediterranean Diet and Fruit and Vegetable Consumption with Subjective Well-being among adults with overweight and obesity. Nutrients. 2021;13(4). 
                  https://doi.org/10.3390/nu13041342
                  
                ."), [43](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1186/s12889-024-17880-9#ref-CR43 "Moreno-Agostino D, Felix Caballero F, Martin-Maria N, Tyrovolas S, Lopez-Garcia P, Rodriguez-Artalejo F, et al. Mediterranean diet and wellbeing: evidence from a nationwide survey. Psychol Health. 2019;34(3):321–35. 
                  https://doi.org/10.1080/08870446.2018.1525492
                  
                .")]. Given the regional differences in diets around the world [[44](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1186/s12889-024-17880-9#ref-CR44 "Ibarrola-Rivas M-J, Nonhebel S. Regional food preferences influence environmental impacts of diets. Food Secur. 2022;14(4):1063–83. 
                  https://doi.org/10.1007/s12571-022-01270-3
                  
                .")], conventional healthy dietary patterns such as the Mediterranean diet or Healthy Eating Index may not adequately align with the dietary structure of Chinese residents. The Chinese Dietary Guidelines (CDG) serves as official dietary guidelines specifically developed to promote healthy and habitual food choices, reduce the risk of chronic diseases, and enhance public health [[45](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1186/s12889-024-17880-9#ref-CR45 "Wang S-s, Lay S, Yu H-n. Shen S-r. Dietary guidelines for Chinese residents (2016): comments and comparisons. J Zhejiang University-SCIENCE B. 2016;17(9):649–56. 
                  https://doi.org/10.1631/jzus.B1600341
                  
                .")]. The CDG recommends a diet that emphasizes whole grains, vegetables, and fruits while advocating for moderate consumption of meat, poultry, eggs, and dairy products [[45](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1186/s12889-024-17880-9#ref-CR45 "Wang S-s, Lay S, Yu H-n. Shen S-r. Dietary guidelines for Chinese residents (2016): comments and comparisons. J Zhejiang University-SCIENCE B. 2016;17(9):649–56. 
                  https://doi.org/10.1631/jzus.B1600341
                  
                .")]. Previous research has extensively assessed the effects of adhering to the Chinese Dietary Guidelines (CDG) on physical and mental health [[34](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1186/s12889-024-17880-9#ref-CR34 "Zang J, Guo C, Wang Z, Cheng Y, Jin W, Zhu Z, et al. Is adherence to the Chinese Dietary guidelines associated with better self-reported health? The Chinese dietary guidelines adherence score. Asia Pac J Clin Nutr. 2018;27(4):914–24. 
                  https://doi.org/10.6133/apjcn.072018.02
                  
                ."), [46](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1186/s12889-024-17880-9#ref-CR46 "Lin J-C, Yin K-L, Huang Y, Liu Y. The HealthyDietary behavioral intention for Chinese residents andIts Effect on depressive symptoms. Chin J Appl Psychol. 2023;29(2):128–36. 
                  https://doi.org/10.20058/j.cnki.cjap.021148
                  
                ."), [47](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1186/s12889-024-17880-9#ref-CR47 "Ding Y, Xu F, Zhong C, Tong L, Li F, Li Q, et al. Association between Chinese Dietary guidelines Compliance Index for pregnant women and risks of pregnancy complications in the Tongji Maternal and Child Health Cohort. Nutrients. 2021;13(3). 
                  https://doi.org/10.3390/nu13030829
                  
                .")]. However, the relationship between CDG adherence and SWB remains unexplored.

Therefore, the aim of the present study is to evaluate the association between adherence to the CDG and its components with evaluative SWB using a cross-sectional survey and a daily diary investigation. Considering the aforementioned health benefits of the healthy dietary pattern, we hypothesize that CDG adherence is also positively associated with SWB in the general population. The present study was approved by the Ethics Committee of ethics committee at Applied Psychology Program, Faculty of Education, Yunnan Normal University (2022010). Written informed consent form was obtained from all of the participants. The procedures conducted in this study adhered to the ethical standards set by the responsible committee on human experimentation (institutional and regional) and conformed to the principles outlined in the Helsinki Declaration of 1964 and all subsequent revisions.

## Materials and methods

### Study 1—the cross-sectional survey

#### Participants and procedure

From October to November 2022, a study was conducted among 1,452 Chinese college students from 8 public universities located in southern China. The study employed a convenience sampling method for data collection, utilizing a combination of online and on-site surveys. Investigators received standardized and uniform training, attaining proficiency in guiding language, questionnaire content, and precautions. Surveys were then conducted both online and on-site by assigned personnel at each school. Participants completed the questionnaires using either online links or hard-copy materials.

After the informed consent process, participants answered some basic demographic questions and self-reported weight and height information. Subsequently, self-reported data on adherence to the CDG and SWB were collected. Questionnaires were counterbalanced in terms of their order to mitigate potential order biases. Following exclusion of individuals without demographic information the remaining 1433 participants aged 17 to 28 years old (average age: 19.19 ± 1.32, 57.0% female) were included for analysis.

### Study variables and measures

Adherence to the Chinese Dietary Guidelines was assessed with the China Prime Diet Quality Score (CPDQS) [[48](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1186/s12889-024-17880-9#ref-CR48 "He Y, Wang H, Fang Y, Xia J, Lian Y, Su C. China prime diet quality score. Wei Sheng Yan jiu = Journal of Hygiene Research. 2021;50(2):198–204. 
                  https://doi.org/10.19813/j.cnki.weishengyanjiu.2021.02.006
                  
                .")]. The CPDQS is a food-based score designed to reflect the diet quality of individuals based on adherence to the 2016 Chinese Dietary Guidelines [[48](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1186/s12889-024-17880-9#ref-CR48 "He Y, Wang H, Fang Y, Xia J, Lian Y, Su C. China prime diet quality score. Wei Sheng Yan jiu = Journal of Hygiene Research. 2021;50(2):198–204. 
                  https://doi.org/10.19813/j.cnki.weishengyanjiu.2021.02.006
                  
                .")]. Dietary intakes of individuals, based on an average of 24-h recalls and brief questionnaire items, were scored according to 22 food groups. These groups encompass 15 recommended dietary components (dark green leafy vegetables, deep orange, other vegetables vegetables, deep orange fruits, citrus fruits, other fruits, whole grains/legumes, sweet potato, other potatoes, soybean, nuts, poultry, fish and shrimp, milk, and eggs) and 7 dietary components should be limited (red meat, fried food, refined grains, sugar sweetered beverages, salt, cooking oil, and alcohol). The CPDQS sums up scores from all 22 food groups, with a score range of 0 to 100 points. A higher score indicating better diet quality. Based on Chinese Dietary Guidelines and Chinese Food Pagoda, the present study classified food groups as (1) cereals and tubers; (2) vegetables and fruits; (3) dairy/soy/nuts; (4) animal source food; and (5) condiments/alcoholic beverages [[45](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1186/s12889-024-17880-9#ref-CR45 "Wang S-s, Lay S, Yu H-n. Shen S-r. Dietary guidelines for Chinese residents (2016): comments and comparisons. J Zhejiang University-SCIENCE B. 2016;17(9):649–56. 
                  https://doi.org/10.1631/jzus.B1600341
                  
                .")]. Further details about the scoring criteria for CPDQS are presented in the subsequent paragraph.

One serving is defined as the highest value of the daily recommended intake based on the recommended amounts of various food groups in the Chinese Food Pagoda, with an energy intake of 2000 kcal. In the scoring system for recommended dietary components, the highest score is attained when reaching 60% of the daily recommended intake. The baseline score ranges are as follows: 0 points for 0 servings, 1 point for 0–0.2 servings, 2 points for 0.2–0.4 servings, 3 points for 0.4–0.6 servings, and 4 points for ≥ 0.6 servings. Among these food groups, dark green leafy vegetables, whole grains/legumes, soybean, and fish/shrimp have scoring values that are twice the baseline score, while sweet potatoes and other potatoes have scoring values that are 0.5 times the baseline score. In the scoring system for dietary components should be limited, the highest score is attained when the intake stays below the daily recommended amount. The baseline score ranges are as follows: 4 points for ≤ 1 serving, 3 point for 1–2 servings, 2 points for 2–3 servings, 1 point for 3–4 servings, 0 points for ≥ 4 servings.

For accurate measurement of the CPDQS, this study referenced the common food types and portion sizes provided by the CDG and the Chinese Food Composition Tables [[45](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1186/s12889-024-17880-9#ref-CR45 "Wang S-s, Lay S, Yu H-n. Shen S-r. Dietary guidelines for Chinese residents (2016): comments and comparisons. J Zhejiang University-SCIENCE B. 2016;17(9):649–56. 
                  https://doi.org/10.1631/jzus.B1600341
                  
                ."), [49](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1186/s12889-024-17880-9#ref-CR49 "Yang Y-X. China Food Composition Tables, Standard Edition. Vol. 2. Di 6 ban edn. Beijing: Peking University Medical Press; 2019.")], along with the price list and actual portion sizes of meals in the refectories of surveyed universities, to annotate the common foods, food portions, and classification criteria for each food group.

SWB was measured by the Index of Well-being (IWB) [[50](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1186/s12889-024-17880-9#ref-CR50 "Campbell A. Subjective measures of well-being. Am Psychol. 1976;31(2):117–24. 
                  https://doi.org/10.1037//0003-066x.31.2.117
                  
                .")]. The Index of Well-Being (IWB) is a widely used measure to assess SWB of Chinese individuals [[51](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1186/s12889-024-17880-9#ref-CR51 "Liu H-h, Peng F, Zeng X-h, Zhao J-b, Zhang X-y. Authoritarian personality and subjective well-being in Chinese college students: the moderation effect of the organizational culture context. Pers Indiv Differ. 2019;138:79–83. 
                  https://doi.org/10.1016/j.paid.2018.09.030
                  
                .")]. It consists of two subsections: the index of general affect and the overall life satisfaction item (α = 0.932). The index of general affect comprises eight items that inquire about the frequency of different emotions experienced, rated on a 7-point scale ranging from 1 (very dissatisfied) to 7 (very satisfied). The overall life satisfaction item is a single question that asks “How satisfied are you with your life as a whole?” and is scored on a 7-point Likert scale (1 = very dissatisfied, 7 = very satisfied). Index of Well-Being = 1.1 * (overall life satisfaction item) + 1.0 * (Index of General Affect).

Demographic covariates included age, gender, registered residence and university information. Health covariates included body mass index (BMI) measured through questions about height and weight. We followed the criteria of the World Health Organization for BMI categories [[52](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1186/s12889-024-17880-9#ref-CR52 "Obesity. Preventing and managing the global epidemic. Report of a WHO consultation. World Health Organ Tech Rep Ser. 2000;894:i–xii.")]: underweight (BMI ≤ 18.49), normal weight (BMI = 18.50 to 24.90), overweight (BMI = 25.00 to 29.90) and obesity (BMI ≥ 30.00).

### Statistical analysis

Analyses were conducted using IBM SPSS 24 Statistics for Windows. First, frequency analysis and descriptive statistics (n and % for categorical variables, and mean and standard deviation (M ± SD) values for continuous variables) were calculated. Next, to explore the relationships between variables, a correlation analysis over all variables was conducted. The following steps of the multiple regression analyses were conducted to examine the predictive role of CDG adherence and its components on SWB. Specifically, three multiple regression models were built for SWB variable considered as a criterion. Model 1 included only four covariate variables: gender, age, registered residence, and BMI; model 2 added CDG adherence as a simultaneous predictor; and model 3 replaced CDG adherence with its individual components, including cereals/tubers, vegetables/fruits, dairy/soy/nuts, animal source food and condiments/alcoholic beverages. For all analyses a p value of < 0.05 was considered significant.

### Study 2—Daily diary investigation

#### Participants and procedure

Study 2 conducted a daily diary study to confirm the findings of study 1 and enhance the robustness of the test of the proposed relationships because the cross-sectional survey data limited the possibility of causality inferences. In November 2022, using the method of snowball sampling via social-networking, 120 students were recruited from 2 universities located in southern China. The survey was administered online, and participants received the questionnaires through Internet links on a specific social media platform. Participants who wanted to take part in the study were invited to sign a written informed consent form and complete a questionnaire aimed at collecting demographic and baseline data. After completing an initial survey, participants took part in a 10-day daily diary study during which they were requested to complete one daily questionnaire on CDG adherence and daily SWB. The diaries were distributed to participants via Internet links every evening at 8 PM. Subsequently, participants were instructed to complete the daily diary by midnight each day.

Five participants who had insufficient data to calculate time-lagged variables for study analyses were excluded. The final sample for analysis comprised 115 students aged 17 to 24 years (mean age: 19.17 ± 1.13), consisting of 56.5% females. This sample consisted of participants who provided baseline data and a minimum of two daily diaries. In total, the 115 participants provided data for 1020 days out of a potential 1150 days (115 participants×10 days), resulting in a response rate of 88.70%.

### Study variables and measures

The baseline questionnaire was aimed at measuring the demographic covariates and baseline SWB. Demographic covariates included age, gender, registered residence and university information. We measured baseline SWB with the Index of Well-being (IWB) identical to those for Study 1 [[50](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1186/s12889-024-17880-9#ref-CR50 "Campbell A. Subjective measures of well-being. Am Psychol. 1976;31(2):117–24. 
                  https://doi.org/10.1037//0003-066x.31.2.117
                  
                .")]. Similar to Study 1, we utilized the CPQDS to assess participants’ adherence to the CDG. Furthermore, participants indicated their daily SWB using a single-item measure included in a comprehensive daily emotion assessment adapted from the Affect Valuation Index (AVI) [[53](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1186/s12889-024-17880-9#ref-CR53 "Tsai JL, Knutson B, Fung HH. Cultural variation in affect valuation. J Pers Soc Psychol. 2006;90(2):288–307. 
                  https://doi.org/10.1037/0022-3514.90.2.288
                  
                .")]. Participants rated how much they had felt “Happy” over the course of the day on a 7-point scale (1 = not at all; 7 = very much). Previous research commonly employs single-item indicators to measure happiness, demonstrating that measuring SWB with a single item is reliable, valid, and viable [[54](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1186/s12889-024-17880-9#ref-CR54 "Dakin BC, Tan NP, Conner TS, Bastian B. The relationship between prosociality, meaning, and happiness in Everyday Life. J Happiness Stud. 2022;23(6):2787–804. 
                  https://doi.org/10.1007/s10902-022-00526-1
                  
                ."), [55](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1186/s12889-024-17880-9#ref-CR55 "Oishi S. The Cornerstone of Research on Subjective Well-Being. Valid Assessment Methodology. In.; 2019.")].

### Statistical analysis

Analyses were conducted using IBM SPSS 24 and Mplus 8.4. First, descriptive statistics and correlation analyses over all variables were calculated by using SPSS 24. In addition, hierarchical multilevel regression was used to examine the hypothesized relationships between CDG adherence and its components and daily SWB. Hierarchical regression allows for within-person and between-person analyses to be conducted simultaneously while adjusting for the autocorrelation of the observations, thus reducing the possibility of inflated results [[56](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1186/s12889-024-17880-9#ref-CR56 "Hox JJ, Moerbeek M, Schoot R. Multilevel analysis: techniques and applications. Third edition edn. New York, NY: Routledge New York, NY; 2018.")]. Hierarchical regression equations were specified using Mplus 8.4, employing restricted maximum likelihood computations. Within-person variables were person-centered, and between-person variables were grand mean-centered.

args.summary:
This is a research article published in BMC Public Health (Volume 24, article number 445, 12 February 2024) titled "Adhere to the Chinese dietary guidelines associated with better subjective well-being: evidence from a cross-sectional survey and a daily diary investigation."

**Purpose:** The study investigates the association between adherence to the Chinese Dietary Guidelines (CDG) and subjective well-being (SWB).

**Methods:** Two studies were conducted:
1. A cross-sectional survey of 1,433 students from 8 universities in southern China (October-November 2020). Adherence to CDG was measured by the China Prime Diet Quality Score (CPDQS, 0-100 points). SWB was measured by the Index of Well-being (IWB) and Affect Valuation Index (AVI).
2. A daily diary investigation of 115 students from 2 universities (November 2022), collecting 10-day daily data (1,020 valid matched responses).

**Key Results:**
- Cross-sectional survey: Significant predictors of SWB included CDG adherence (β=0.24, p<0.001) and its components: cereals/tubers (β=0.07, p=0.024), vegetables/fruits (β=0.11, p<0.001), dairy/soy/nuts (β=0.11, p=0.002), and condiments/alcoholic beverages (β=0.08, p=0.002).
- Daily diary investigation: Positive associations between CDG adherence (β=0.19, p<0.001) and components: vegetables/fruits (β=0.11, p=0.001), dairy/soy/nuts (β=0.06, p=0.009), animal source food (β=0.06, p=0.026), and condiments/alcoholic beverages (β=0.07, p=0.026) with higher daily SWB.

**Conclusions:** Adherence to healthy dietary patterns like the CDG, rather than focusing on individual components, is associated with better SWB. The study offers modest evidence supporting the role of the CDG in promoting positive mental health. The CDG recommends whole grains, vegetables, and fruits while advocating moderate consumption of meat, poultry, eggs, and dairy products. This research is important because most prior studies focused on Mediterranean diet and were limited by cross-sectional designs.

# 关于老年人的营养与健康 那些你应该知道的事儿

2024-05-23 12:55:03  来源：新华网

新华网北京5月23日电（张欣烁）国家统计局公布的数据显示，截至2023年末，中国60岁及以上人口超2.9亿，占全国人口的21.1%，其中65岁及以上人口超2.1亿，占全国人口的15.4%。如何让每位老年人安度晚年，安享温暖愉悦的“夕阳红”，已经成为全社会普遍关心的话题。

  为增强老年人营养健康意识，提升老年人营养健康素养，促进老年人形成健康生活方式，近日，新华网采访了几位营养专家，听一听专业营养师们对老年人的营养健康给出了哪些建议。

合肥市营养学会执行会长凌以耸

**预防慢病 营养是关键**

  《“十四五”国民健康规划》提出，到2025年，中国人均预期寿命在2020年的77.93岁基础上继续提高1岁左右。到2035年，人均预期寿命达到80岁以上。

  随着长寿时代的来临，一些新问题与新挑战也随之而来，合肥市营养学会执行会长凌以耸表示：“这个时代普遍高寿，正是因为普遍高寿，所以迎来一个新的问题，就是慢病高发，因为很多慢病都属于退行性疾病。”

  退行性疾病一般情况下是指随着年龄的增长，身体器官老化出现的病变。与普通的疾病不同，慢病一般很难通过吃药、开刀等医疗手段获得康复，唯一的办法就是预防，或者说延缓疾病的进程，减少相关并发症的发生。

  适量的运动、充足的睡眠、心理平衡以及合理膳食是健康的四大基石。凌以耸认为，预防慢病需要从健康的生活方式,以及合理的膳食安排入手。“我们在提合理膳食的时候，可能很多人认为就是吃普通的饭菜，其实合理膳食的重点在于营养均衡。营养均衡的手段很多，可以通过一日三餐也可以通过合理的营养强化营养补充。”

  “为什么老年人都怕摔跤？”凌以耸举例说，“是因为老年人的骨头比较容易骨折，而骨折的一个重要原因就是很多老人都存在的骨质疏松的问题。骨质疏松与钙、胶原蛋白、维生素C、维生素D这些营养素的缺乏有密切关系。如果这些营养素补充得比较充分，再加上合理的锻炼，他的骨质就可以保持相当长一段时间都是健康的。”

首都保健营养美食学会营养配餐专业委员会会长叶明珏

**老年人的十大膳食建议**

  随着年龄的增长，身体的代谢能力和吸收能力逐渐下降，因此，老年人需要更加精细地规划自己的饮食，确保身体能够获得全面而均衡的营养支持。合理膳食不仅有助于老年人保持健康的体重和体态，还能提高生活质量，延缓身体的衰老过程。

  对此，首都保健营养美食学会营养配餐专业委员会会长叶明珏针对老年人的饮食规划提出了十点建议：

  一、主食以谷类为主，要注意粗细的搭配。全谷物或者粗粮的摄入量建占到三分之一到二分之一，可以煮得软烂一点，有利于消化和吸收。。

  二、摄入一些鱼禽肉蛋类的食物，每天在120到150克左右，保证优质蛋白质占到膳食总蛋白供应量的50%以上。

  三、摄入适量的奶类、大豆或者及其制品。老年人每天去喝300到400毫升左右的鲜牛奶，或相当量的奶制品或奶酪、酸奶等。大豆或者豆制品可以选择豆腐、豆浆、豆腐干等。

  四、餐餐有蔬菜，每天有水果。建议老年人要多吃一些深色的蔬菜以及十字花科类的蔬菜，因为这些蔬菜当中含有丰富的维生素和矿物质。每天的蔬菜摄入量在300到400克左右，水果摄入量100到200克。

  五、注意饮食清淡，做到少油限盐。每天的烹饪油控制在20到25克，建议轮换着吃各种植物油，不提倡吃单一种类植物油。

  六、主动饮水，白开水为主。每天的饮水量在1.5升到1.7升左右，视老年人的运动情况而定。

  七、限量饮酒，酒精摄入量建议每天不超过15克，心脑血管疾病的老年人建议尽量不要饮酒。

  八、少量多餐，更有利于食物的消化和吸收。

  九、营造温馨愉快的进餐环境以及良好的氛围，心情愉悦可以使食物的营养价值发挥得更好，更有利于营养吸收。

  十、当老年人咀嚼能力以及消化吸收能力下降的时候，可以在营养师或医生的建议下，合理地选择膳食营养的补充剂以弥补人体所需的营养和热量缺口。

长沙市健康管理学会理事长沈春芳

**合理应用营养补充剂**

  通过合理摄入营养补充剂，老年人可以有效弥补日常饮食中可能存在的营养不足，满足身体对营养的全面需求。这不仅能够增强老年人的免疫力，预防疾病的发生，还能帮助他们维持良好的身体状态，提高生活质量。

  今年1月15日，国务院办公厅发布《关于发展银发经济增进老年人福祉的意见》（以下称《意见》），这是首个以“银发经济”命名的文件。《意见》提出，鼓励研发适合老年人咀嚼吞咽和营养要求的保健食品、特殊医学用配方食品。

  长沙市健康管理学会理事长沈春芳认为，由于老年人的身体机能处于下行状态，消化和吸收功能也较差，如果能够根据老年人的身体状况研发出符合老年群体特点的营养产品，会更容易被市场所接受。

  同时，很多老年人在面对营养补充剂等产品时，由于营养专业知识的缺乏，常常容易陷入误区。对此，沈春芳给出了几点需要注意的问题：首先，产品的安全性和合规性是最重要的，要从正规渠道购买可靠的产品。其次，要根据自身健康状况和营养需求选择产品，不要盲目跟风过度补充，从而增加身体负担。再次，要注意产品的成分与剂量，要按照产品的推荐的剂量和使用方法去摄入产品。

北京市营养学会副秘书长、常务理事程洁

**产业发展教育先行**

  随着银发经济蓬勃发展，养老领域的新业态不断涌现。陪诊师、健康照护师、医疗护理员等大量新兴职业需求接踵而至，但是与老年人的需要相比仍然存在较大的差距，供给总量不足和结构失衡问题还比较突出。

  这些新职业、新岗位的人才如何培养？如何对他们进行评价？如何对他们进行后续的发展规划？

  北京市营养学会副秘书长、常务理事程洁表示：“新岗位、新技能在很多领域都在出现，原有的标准已经不能满足产业对人才的需求，这时就需要有大量的社会团体、协会，包括其他一些组织站出来，跟产业中的企业合作，共同开发标准，标准一旦形成了就有了人才的培养方案，我们就可以去开展相关新岗位新技能人才的培养。产业发展教育先行，我们需要在人才端去提升质量、去扩容，来更好地满足人才发展。”

  除了满足老年人的康养需求、日常生活需求以外，关爱老年人的心理健康，满足老年人精神文化需求，丰盈老年人精神生活，减少老年人心灵的孤独感、消沉感、苦闷感也是提高老年人的生活品质、让老年人的晚年生活更美好的重要举措。

  关爱老年人需要政府、企业、组织机构还有个人同心协力。为此，新华网与雀巢健康科学于今年一月联合发起了“桑榆计划”暨中国健康老人“佳”分行动，鼓励老人走出家门，加大社会参与，通过帮助老年人拥有健康的体魄和积极向上的精神风貌，助力提升老年人生活品质、传递文化精神、传播榜样力量，让“美好的生活方式”得以延续。

  在后续活动中，“桑榆计划”将从行动、文化、营养健康三个纬度，开展City Walk（城市漫步）城市线路征集、City Walk城市传统文化代言、City Walk营养健康大讲堂系列城市文化活动。立足社区，多城联动，组织全国“健康老人”走出去、多锻炼，在探寻城市文化脉络的过程中锻炼体魄，培养积极乐观的心态。

This article from Xinhua News, published on May 23, 2024, addresses nutrition and health for older adults in China, where over 2.9 billion people are aged 60+ (21.1% of the population). It features insights from multiple nutrition experts on preventing chronic diseases through diet, and provides practical dietary recommendations for seniors.

Key points include:
- **Prevention of chronic diseases** (凌以耸, Hefei Nutrition Society): Chronic diseases are age-related degenerative conditions that cannot be cured through medicine alone; prevention via balanced nutrition, exercise, sleep, and mental health is critical. Osteoporosis in seniors is linked to deficiencies in calcium, collagen, vitamin C, and vitamin D.
- **Ten dietary recommendations** (叶明珏, Capital Health Nutrition Society): (1) Whole grains as 1/3–1/2 of staple foods; (2) 120–150g of animal protein daily; (3) 300–400ml of milk or dairy products; (4) 300–400g vegetables and 100–200g fruits daily; (5) Limit cooking oil to 20–25g and salt; (6) Drink 1.5–1.7L of water; (7) Limit alcohol to ≤15g/day; (8) Eat smaller, more frequent meals; (9) Enjoy pleasant mealtime environments; (10) Consider nutritional supplements when chewing/digestion declines.
- **Nutritional supplements** (沈春芳, Changsha Health Management Society): The State Council's January 2024 "Silver Economy" policy encourages supplements for seniors. Seniors should buy from reliable sources, choose based on health needs, and follow recommended dosages.
- **Education and workforce development** (程洁, Beijing Nutrition Society): New professions (e.g., health caregivers, medical assistants) are needed; industry standards and training programs must be developed through collaboration between associations and enterprises.
- **"桑榆计划" (Sangyu Plan)**: A joint initiative by Xinhua and Nestlé Health Science launched in January 2024 to encourage seniors to be more active through City Walk activities, cultural events, and nutrition education across multiple cities.

中国居民膳食指南解读

# 专家解读|新版膳食指南（五）少盐少油，控糖限酒

发布时间：2016-09-30 点击次数：

**作者：翟凤英**《 中国居民膳食指南（2016）》修订专家委员会副主任委员、中国疾控中心营养所 教授

**关键推荐**

◇ 培养清淡饮食习惯，少吃高盐和油炸食品。成人每天食盐不超过6g，每天烹调油25~30g。

◇ 控制添加糖的摄入量，每天摄入不超过50g，最好控制在约25克以下。

◇ 每日反式脂肪酸摄入量不超过2g。

◇ 足量饮水，成年人每天7~8杯（1500~1700ml），提倡饮用白开水和茶水；不喝或少喝含糖饮料。

◇ 儿童少年、孕妇、乳母不应饮酒。成人如饮酒，男性一天饮用酒的酒精量不超过25g，女性不超过15g。

**盐**

**一、我们为什么要少吃盐**

大多菜肴以咸作基础味，是食盐让我们享受到了美味佳肴。高血压流行病学调查证实，人群的血压水平和高血压的患病率均与食盐的摄入量密切相关。50岁以上的人、有家族性高血压的人、超重和肥胖者，其血压对食盐摄入量的变化更为敏感，膳食中的食盐如果增加，发生心脑血管意外的危险性就大大增加。

中国营养学会建议健康成年人一天食盐（包括酱油和其他食物中的食盐量）的摄入量是不超过6克。但2012年的调查显示，我国居民每人日平均摄入食盐10.5克。因此，减少食盐量仍需努力。

**二、如何减少盐摄入量**

首先要自觉纠正因口味过咸而过量添加食盐和酱油的不良习惯，对每天食盐摄入采取总量控制，用量具量出，每餐按量放入菜肴。

一般20mL酱油中含有3克食盐，10克蛋黄酱含1.5克食盐，如果菜肴需要用酱油和酱类，应按比例减少食盐用量。

习惯过咸味食物者，为满足口感的需要，可在烹制菜肴时放少许醋，提高菜肴的鲜香味，帮助自己适应少盐食物。

烹制菜肴时如果加糖会掩盖咸味，所以不能仅凭品尝来判断食盐是否过量,使用量具更准确。此外，还要注意减少酱菜、腌制食品以及其他过咸食品的摄入量。

**油**

**一、烹调油的两面性**

类饮食离不开油，烹调油除了可以增加食物的风味，还是人体必需脂肪酸和维生素E的重要来源，并且有助于食物中脂溶性维生素的吸收利用。但是过多脂肪摄入会增加慢性疾病发生的风险。

**二、如何科学用油**

科学用油包括“少用油”和“巧用油”，即控制烹调油的食用总量不超过30克/天，并且搭配多种植物油，尽量少食用动物油和人造黄油或起酥油。

**“少用油”小窍门**

使用带刻度的油壶来控制炒菜用油；选择合理的烹饪方法，如蒸、煮、炖、拌等，使用煎炸代替油炸；少吃富含饱和脂肪和反式脂肪酸的食物，例如饼干、蛋糕、糕点、加工肉制品以及薯条/薯片等。

**怎么“巧用油”**

动物油的饱和脂肪酸比例较高；植物油则以不饱和脂肪酸为主。不同植物油又各具特点，如橄榄油、茶油、菜籽油的单不饱和脂肪酸含量较高，玉米油、葵花籽油则富含亚油酸，胡麻油（亚麻籽油）中富含a-亚麻酸。因此应当经常更换烹调油的种类，食用多种植物油，减少动物油的用量。

**添加糖**

**一、为什么控制添加糖**

添加糖是指人工加入到食品中的糖类，包括饮料中的糖，具有甜味特征，常见的有白砂糖、绵白糖、冰糖和红糖。添加糖是纯能量食物，不含其他营养成分，过多摄入会增加龋齿及超重肥胖发生的风险。因此，**平衡膳食中不要求添加糖，若需要摄入建议每天摄入量不超过50g，最好控制在约25g以下。**

**二、如何控制添加糖摄入量**

对于儿童青少年来说，含糖饮料是添加糖的主要来源，建议不喝或少喝含糖饮料。添加糖的另外一个主要来源是包装食品如糕点、甜点、冷饮等，减少此类食品的摄入，也可控制添加糖。此外，家庭烹饪时也会使用糖作为佐料加入菜肴中，如红烧、糖醋等，在烹饪时应注意尽量少加糖。喝茶、咖啡时也容易摄入过多的糖，需要引起注意。

**酒**

**一、为什么要限酒**

酒虽然是我们饮食文化的一部分，但是从营养学的角度看，酒中没有任何营养元素。有许多科学证据证明酒精是造成肝损伤、胎儿酒精综合征、痛风、结直肠癌、乳腺癌、心血管疾病的危险因素。此外，由于酒含有较多的能量，特别是高度白酒，经常饮酒会造成能量过剩；同时，酒会影响食物营养素的吸收，造成营养素缺乏。

还有对于孕妇、乳母、儿童少年、特殊状况或特定职业人群以及驾驶机动工具的人员，即使少量饮酒也会对健康、工作或生活造成不良影响。

**二、如何做到限酒**

从健康的考虑出发，男性和女性成年人每日饮酒应该不超过酒精25克和15克。换算成不同酒类，25克酒精相当于啤酒750ml，葡萄酒250ml，38°白酒75克，高度白酒50克；15克酒精相当于啤酒450ml，葡萄酒150ml，38°白酒50克，高度白酒30克。

This webpage is a section of the Chinese Dietary Guidelines (2016 edition) website, specifically an expert interpretation article on Guideline #5: "Less salt, less oil, control added sugar, limit alcohol." Published on September 30, 2016, the article is authored by Zhai Fengying, Deputy Chair of the revision expert committee and professor at the Chinese CDC Nutrition Institute.

**Key Recommendations:**
- **Salt:** Adults should consume no more than 6g of salt daily. Chinese average intake is 10.5g (2012 survey). Tips include using measuring tools, compensating with vinegar, and reducing high-salt processed foods.
- **Oil:** Daily cooking oil intake should be 25–30g. Use measuring oil bottles, choose steaming/boiling over frying, and vary plant oil types (olive, corn, flaxseed, etc.) while limiting animal fats and trans fats (max 2g/day).
- **Added Sugar:** Limit to ≤50g/day, ideally ≤25g. Main sources are sugary drinks, packaged sweets, and cooking. No added sugar is required in a balanced diet.
- **Alcohol:** No nutritional value. Adults: men ≤25g alcohol/day, women ≤15g. Equivalent to 750ml beer or 250ml wine for men; 450ml beer or 150ml wine for women. Pregnant women, children, and certain professionals should not drink.
- **Water:** Adults should drink 1500–1700ml (7–8 cups) daily, preferably plain water or tea.

**《中国健康生活方式预防心血管代谢疾病指南》**

心血管代谢疾病包括高血压、糖尿病、血脂异常、冠心病、脑卒中等，严重威胁我国居民健康，疾病负担持续增长。健康的生活方式是预防和管理心血管代谢疾病的重要基石。中华预防医学会，中华预防医学会心脏病预防与控制专业委员会，中华医学会糖尿病学分会，中华预防医学会卒中预防与控制专业委员会，中华医学会健康管理学分会，中华预防医学会慢性病预防与控制分会，中国医疗保健国际交流促进会高血压分会，中国社区卫生协会基于中国人群的研究证据，制定出《中国健康生活方式预防心血管代谢疾病指南》，本文将主要内容提炼，为护理同仁提供参考。

本指南主要基于中国人群的研究证据，针对膳食与饮料、 身体活动、吸烟饮酒等方面提出建议，旨在促进我国居民采取健康的生活方式，预防心血管代谢疾病，推动健康中国行动的实施。

一、膳食营养推荐

(1) 合理膳食可以预防心血管代谢疾病

(2)对于无心血管代谢疾病及其他慢性病的成年人，需保持平衡的膳食营养结构；具体膳食和营养建议见表 1

(3)谷类为主是平衡膳食的基础。增加全谷物、杂粮、杂豆和薯类的摄入，有助于降低心血管代谢疾病发病风险

(4) 增加蔬菜水果的摄入，适量吃鱼类、蛋类、豆制品、乳制品，有助于降低心血管代谢疾病发病风险

(5)减少钠盐的摄入，平均每人每天摄入钠盐＜ 5 g

(6)减少加工肉类、饱和脂肪酸的摄入，控制膳食胆固醇摄入

(7) 减少含糖饮料的摄入，适量饮茶

![](/uploads/image/20200520/20200520094515_7581.png)

1.膳食营养

![](/uploads/image/20200520/20200520094537_9300.png)

（1）谷薯类

谷薯类食物含有丰富的碳水化合物、矿物质、 B 族维生素、膳食纤维等。增加全谷物的摄入有利于降低 2 型糖尿病以及心血管病发病和死亡风险。建议一般成年人每天摄入谷薯类250-400 g，其中包括全谷物和杂豆类 50-150 g，薯类 50-100g。建议每餐有谷类，烹调时“粗细搭配”，如大米与糙米、杂粮（小米、玉米和燕麦等）及杂豆（红小豆、绿豆和芸豆等）搭配食用。

（2）蔬菜与水果

摄入蔬菜水果具有心血管保护作用，增加蔬菜和水果摄入，可降低成年人高血压、脑卒中及主要心血管病发病风险，还有助于绝经早期妇女降低LDL-C水平。建议一般成年人每天摄入 300-500 g 新鲜蔬菜（深色蔬菜 应占一半）， 200-350 g 新鲜水果，果汁不能代替鲜果。

（3）鱼类和禽畜肉类

食用鱼类有助于预防心血管病，建议成年人鱼类摄入每周 300-525 g， 采用煮、蒸等非油炸烹调方法，减少营养素的丢失；每天摄入畜禽类 40-75 g，红肉（如猪、牛、羊肉类）摄入量不宜过多。

（4）蛋类

鸡蛋富含优质蛋白质、维生素和矿物质，但胆固醇含量也较高。建议一般成年人每周摄入鸡蛋 3-6 个。对高胆固醇血症和心血管病高危人群，建议每天膳食胆固醇摄入小于 300 mg（约 1 个鸡蛋黄）

（5）大豆及坚果类

大豆中富含蛋白质、膳食纤维、钾、钙等营养素。食用豆制品和坚果有助于降低心血管病发病风险和全因死亡风险。目前建议每周适量食用坚果 50-70 g。

（6）奶类及乳制品

  奶类等乳制品种类多样，是膳食钙和蛋白质的重要来源。每天饮用牛奶可降低心血管病发病和死亡风险。建议可以摄入不同种类的奶制品，约合每天 150-300 g 的液态奶。

（7）茶、含糖饮料和咖啡

多年长期保持饮茶习惯有助于预防心血管病，糖尿病发病风险降低 20%。但是，长期饮浓茶会影响铁的吸收，睡前饮浓茶可能造成兴奋而影响睡眠。建议一般成年人适量饮茶，每月茶叶消耗量为 50-250 g， 绿茶为佳，不喝或少喝含糖饮料。建议饮用咖啡与进餐时间最好相隔半小时以上，以免影响食物中的钙、铁、维生素B6的吸收。

（8）钠盐

限制钠盐摄入不仅可以预防高血压，也有助于降低心血管病发病和死亡风险。日常生活中应注意烹饪时少放盐或其他富含钠的调料（如酱油、味精、 鱼露等），并控制餐桌上的用盐量，养成清淡饮食的习惯。既往我国多个专业学会指南均推荐提倡人均每天食盐摄入量不高于 5 g，与 WHO 的推荐标准一致。

（9）辣椒素及辣膳食

辣椒富含维生素 C，也含有较高的维生素 B、β胡萝卜素以及钙、铁等矿物质，其活性成分为辣椒素。辣膳食有助于增加盐味觉，减少摄盐量、降低血压，降低心血管病和全因死亡风险。

（10）复合维生素及脂肪酸

建议一般人群通过膳食多样化来摄入维生素、矿物质，不建议单独服用膳食补充剂；孕妇等特殊人群服用膳食补充剂前请咨询医生。推荐一般成年人多食用富含不饱和脂肪酸的食物，例如：鱼、菜籽油、 橄榄油等。食用油摄入每天不超过 20 g（约 2 瓷勺），应选择多品种食用油并经常调换，而心血管病高风险的个体需控制总脂肪摄入量。

2.特定人群膳食推荐

（1）对65岁以上老年人的膳食指导

![](/uploads/image/20200520/20200520094659_7582.png)

首先要保证食物多样化、营养充足，保持适宜体重，不要过于消瘦。对消化能力明显降低的老年人，可少量多餐、进食细软食物；老年人对缺水的耐受性下降，应主动饮水，每天饮水量达到1500-1700 ml。 老年人身体代谢机能减慢，更应注意饮食清淡，避免高盐和油炸食品，控制甜食摄入；浓肉汤、海鲜浓汤等富含嘌呤类的饮食，易诱发高尿酸血症和痛风，也需控制。老年人需积极进行户外活动、接受紫外线照射，有利于体内维生素 D 的合成和延缓骨质疏松。

（2）对代谢风险升高人群的膳食指导

![](/uploads/image/20200520/20200520094718_2426.png)

1)血压升高个体

对血压升高的个体，更需要重视限制钠盐的摄入，除了减少烹饪时添加的食盐，还要减少使用含钠的调味品（酱油、味精、鱼露等），长期口味偏重、高盐饮食容易诱发心血管病。另外，少吃加工类食物（如糕点、火腿、罐头等），这些食物通常高脂、高糖、高盐。推荐多吃蔬菜、水果、低脂乳制品、鱼、全谷类、纤维类、富含钾和其他矿物质食物，同时减少红肉和加工肉类、饱和脂肪酸、胆固醇、添加糖和钠的摄入，有利于控制血压。

2)血脂异常个体

对于血脂异常的个体，需要控制膳食胆固醇摄入，更应限制摄入富含饱和脂肪酸的食物，包括大部分饼干、糕点、薯条、土豆片等油炸食品和加工零食，这些食物的制作过程往往会使用（人造）黄油和奶油、可可脂等，容易含有较高的饱和脂肪酸以及反式脂肪酸。烹调油选择菜籽油、玉米油、葵花籽油、橄榄油等 植物油，并调换使用。

3)糖代谢异常个体

对于糖代谢异常者，需要在专业营养（医）师或团队指导下接受个体化医学营养治疗，在全面评估个体营养状况前提下调整总能量的摄入，使血糖、血压、血脂达标。糖尿病患者长期服用二甲双胍者应预防维生素 B12 缺乏。目前尚不推荐食用含有复合维生素、矿物质、鱼油等成分的保健品来控制血糖或预防心血管病 。

二 、身体活动推荐

1.所有人都应当增加运动、减少久坐，即使少量增加身体活动也能带来健康获益

2.推荐健康成年人每周进行至少150 min 中等强度或至少 75 min 高强度有氧身体活动，或相当量的两种强度活动的组合；在身体情况允许的情况下，可提高到每周 300 min 中等强度或 150 min 高强度有氧身体活动，或相当量的两种强度活动的组合，但应先科学评估，循序渐进

3.推荐健康成年人每周至少 2 天进行针对所有主要肌肉群的增强肌肉型身体活动，如俯卧撑、 仰卧起坐、深蹲起立等

4.每天睡眠时间保持在 6-8 h

5.中老年居民（尤其 65 岁及以上老年人）、 慢性病患者或残障人士，即使不能达到健康成年人的身体活动量，也应该根据身体状况坚持进行身体活动，避免久坐不动

（1）65 岁及以上老年人的身体活动

![](/uploads/image/20200520/20200520094754_3363.png)

针对健康人群的身体活动推荐，适用于所有老年人，如果不能达到每周150 min中等强度身体活动的目标，则在其身体状况允许范围内尽可能多运动。但是，老年人需要根据自身状况，或经过专业评估，选择合适强度的身体活动。建议老年人按照相对强度的标准选择身体活动类型。另外，建议老年人的运动形式多样化，除有氧运动和增强肌肉型运动外，要增加平衡型活动及柔韧性运动；推荐选择适当的集体运动，如广场舞、健身操等。

（2）患有慢性病者或残障人士的身体活动

规律的身体活动有助于改善慢性病患者或残障人士的生活质量，降低新的疾病发生风险，身体活动能够促进认知功能的恢复、改善心肺功能和肌肉适应性以及提高自理能力。针对一般人群的身体活动推荐，原则上也适用于慢性病患者（冠心病、脑卒中等患者除外）或残障人士。然而，考虑到这部分人群的特殊状况，建议通过咨询专业医师制定适合自身状况的身体活动划；建议残障人士根据自身状况选择不同类型的增强肌肉型身体活动，例如仰卧起坐、深蹲起立等。同时，应当注意运动安全，有条件的情况下可请他人协助。

三、戒烟推荐

1.吸烟是心血管代谢疾病的独立危险因素并且效应较强，推荐避免吸入任何形式的烟草

2.对吸烟者反复提供戒烟建议，帮助其戒烟

3. 避免被动吸烟

4.避免主动或被动吸入电子烟

![](/uploads/image/20200520/20200520094824_4301.png)

戒烟可以降低冠心病、脑卒中等心血管病发病和死亡风险。戒烟后，心血管病发病风险迅速降低，戒烟时间越长，心血管健康获益越大。 鼓励各年龄段吸烟者戒烟。研究表明，30 岁、40 岁 或50岁时戒烟可分别延长约10年、9年或6年的预期寿命。医疗服务机构应当结合吸烟者既往病史和个人情况为其提供专业的戒烟指导，使其了解吸烟危害，戒烟步骤，以及可能遇到的困难和解决办法。同时 动员家人和朋友帮助吸烟者戒烟。此外，各级政府应当制定有效的控烟法规，加大宣传力度，防止青 少年吸烟，减少被动吸烟，为公众创造无烟环境。

四、限制饮酒推荐

1.对于饮酒者应限制每天酒精摄入量：成年男性＜ 25 g，成年女性＜ 15 g；或酒精摄入量每周≤ 100 g。肝肾功能不良、高血压、心房颤动、怀孕者不应饮酒

2.对于糖尿病患者不推荐饮酒，若饮酒应警惕酒精可能引发的低血糖，避免空腹饮酒

3.不建议不饮酒者通过少量饮酒预防心血管病

饮酒与心血管病之间的关系复杂。适量饮酒可以降低缺血性心脏病发生风险。但是，饮酒过量会增加脑卒中、心房颤动和心力衰竭发生风险。考虑到饮酒引起的综合健康风险可能大于潜在的心血管健康获益，因此不建议不饮酒者通过少量饮酒预防心血管病。

This webpage is a summary of the "Chinese Healthy Lifestyle Guidelines for Prevention of Cardiometabolic Diseases" (2020), published on a nursing/healthcare portal. The guidelines were developed by multiple Chinese medical societies and provide evidence-based recommendations for preventing cardiometabolic diseases (hypertension, diabetes, dyslipidemia, coronary heart disease, stroke) through lifestyle modifications.

**Key Dietary Recommendations:**
- Maintain balanced diet with grains as foundation; consume 250-400g of grains daily (including 50-150g whole grains/legumes, 50-100g tubers)
- Eat 300-500g fresh vegetables (half dark-colored) and 200-350g fresh fruit daily
- Consume fish 300-525g weekly; poultry/meat 40-75g daily; limit red meat
- Eat 3-6 eggs per week; limit dietary cholesterol to <300mg for high-risk individuals
- Consume nuts 50-70g weekly and dairy equivalent to 150-300g liquid milk daily
- Limit sodium to <5g salt per day (<1 teaspoon)
- Reduce processed meats, saturated fats, sugar-sweetened beverages; moderate tea drinking
- Use cooking oil ≤20g daily; choose unsaturated oils (canola, olive, etc.)
- No routine dietary supplements for general population

**Specific Population Guidance:**
- Older adults (65+): Ensure nutrient diversity, adequate hydration (1500-1700ml daily), avoid high-salt/fried foods, engage in outdoor activity
- Those with elevated blood pressure: Strictly limit sodium, reduce processed foods, increase potassium-rich foods
- Those with dyslipidemia: Limit saturated and trans fats, choose plant-based cooking oils
- Those with abnormal glucose metabolism: Seek individualized medical nutrition therapy

**Physical Activity Recommendations:**
- At least 150 min moderate-intensity or 75 min vigorous-intensity aerobic activity weekly
- Muscle-strengthening activities at least 2 days per week
- Sleep 6-8 hours daily
- Older adults and those with chronic conditions should remain active within their capabilities

**Smoking:**
- Avoid all forms of tobacco; smoking cessation reduces cardiovascular risk; quitting at age 30, 40, or 50 extends life expectancy by ~10, 9, or 6 years respectively

**Alcohol:**
- Limit daily alcohol: men <25g, women <15g; weekly ≤100g
- Not recommended for those with liver/kidney issues, hypertension, atrial fibrillation, or pregnancy
- Do not start drinking to prevent cardiovascular disease

# 关注“备老人群” 《中国老年人群营养健康问题现状及改善策略研究报告》正式发布

2025-05-26 11:34:59  来源：新华网

新华网北京5月26日电（沈美） 衰老是增龄历程中一个长期持续、缓慢渐进和不可逆转的自然过程，深入探究随着年龄增长人在生理变化、营养膳食行为以及健康状况方面发生的变化，对于延缓衰老、预防慢性疾病、增进老年人健康福祉、提升生活质量意义非凡。

《中国老年人群营养健康问题现状及改善策略研究报告》发布现场（从左至右：中国乳制品工业协会执行理事长刘美菊、中国营养学会秘书长韩军花、利乐公司大中华区企业传播与可持续发展副总裁牟晓燕）

5月23日至25日，中国乳制品工业协会第三十一次年会分论坛中老年营养健康创新技术论坛在南京举办。会上，由中国营养学会编制、利乐公司支持的《中国老年人群营养健康问题现状及改善策略研究报告》（下简称：报告）正式发布。

据了解，报告编纂历时数月，系统梳理了当前我国老年人群不同年龄段的主要营养健康问题，并指出老龄阶段的营养补充应提早规划、科学干预。报告特别强调45至64岁“备老阶段”对于健康老龄化的重要性。在这一阶段的日常营养补充和健康生活习惯的养成，将从源头提升老年期的健康水平与生活质量。

**如何定义“备老人群”？**

在报告中：备老人群定义为45至64岁之间的人群。这个年龄段的大多数“备老人群”仍然还充满活力、思维清晰、消化吸收能力降低还不显著、甚至尚在工作岗位和社会生活中发挥着重要作用，但是衰老已经悄然而至，各项功能退化已经在路上。

根据中国慢性病与营养监测（CNHS）数据，45至64岁备老人群能量及宏量营养素摄入呈现出不同程度的不足和过量。总能量摄入男女性别均略高于《中国居民膳食营养素参考摄入量（2023版）》中低强度身体活动水平的EER推荐值；碳水化合物摄入量超过EAR 推荐量1倍，但其供能比仍在AMDR推荐值50%~65%的范围内；脂肪供能比（男33.7%，女32.6%）均超过《中国居民膳食指南2022》30%的上限；而在备老人群中半数以上人的蛋白质摄入量低于RNI推荐值（男65克，女55克），不足量达到7克或以上。提示需优化膳食供能结构，降低脂肪与碳水化合物比例，并提升优质蛋白摄入。

《中国居民营养与慢性病状况报告（2020）》的数据显示，中国成年人群膳食结构呈现显著的年龄分层特征与地理分布差异。研究显示，45~64岁及以上群体谷薯类摄入量（均值317.2g/d）显著高于年轻群体，但蔬菜（254.4~255.9g/d）和水果（30.9~34.8g/d）摄入量均低于膳食指南推荐下限（300g/d和200g/d），且呈现城乡梯度差异（城市摄入量高于农村p < 0.05）。值得注意的是，乳制品（16.7~23.2g/d）和大豆制品（9.7~9.9g/d）摄入严重不足，仅达到推荐量的5.6%~7.7%和38.8~39.6%，可能导致钙（平均摄入量 < 400mg/d）和优质蛋白质摄入不足。性别分析表明，男性在动物性食物（畜肉+73.5g/d vs.女性+61.2g/d）和烹调油（+42.7g/d vs.女性+38.9g/d）摄入显著偏高（p < 0.01），而女性水果（+34.8g/d vs.男性+28.5g/d）和乳制品（+16.7g/d vs.男性+12.3g/d）摄入相对较高。这种膳食模式差异可能加剧营养失衡相关慢性病的发生风险，特别是心血管疾病和代谢综合征的年龄梯度流行趋势。

**“备老人群”易患哪些疾病？**

报告中提到，50-64岁人群是糖尿病的高发年龄段之一，患病率显著高于年轻人群。这一年龄段的糖尿病患病率约为15%-20%，这一年龄段的人群通常处于代谢综合征的高发期，肥胖、高血压、高血脂等代谢异常显著增加糖尿病风险。工作压力大、饮食不规律、缺乏运动等生活方式因素是糖尿病高发的重要原因。糖尿病相关并发症（如心血管疾病、肾病、视网膜病变等）开始显现，需加强早期筛查和管理。

男性肥胖症患病率在50-54岁达到峰值。根据《中国居民营养与慢性病状况报告（2020年）》，50-64岁人群的超重率和肥胖症患病率较高，尤其是在男性中。肥胖尤其是中心性肥胖是阻塞性睡眠呼吸暂停综合征（OSAS）的重要危险因素。在BMI超过30kg/m²的肥胖症人群中，OSAS患病率高达40%。

近几十年来，我国≥18岁人群的血脂异常患病率显著升高，尤其是在中年阶段（50-64岁），血脂异常的患病率较高。该年龄段人群的低密度脂蛋白胆固醇（LDL-C）水平普遍偏高，且知晓率、治疗率和控制率均处于较低水平。

高血压、糖尿病、肥胖和吸烟等危险因素在这一年龄段较为常见，进一步增加了血脂异常的风险。50-64岁人群是ASCVD的高发年龄段，尤其是男性。ASCVD的总体风险与血脂异常密切相关。该年龄段人群的ASCVD风险评估显示，中危及以上人群比例较高，需重点关注LDL-C的管理。该年龄段人群的血脂异常往往与不健康的生活方式（如高脂饮食、缺乏运动、吸烟等）密切相关，需要通过生活方式干预和药物治疗相结合的方式进行管理。

**“备老人群”如何补充营养？**

研究显示：“备老”年龄段的营养储备尤为重要，这个时期食物摄入、营养补充、慢性病预防、功能维护等健康储备，将能有效的改善人群膳食摄入维生素、矿物质、植物活性有益成分的不足状况，为老年期营养需求奠定坚实基础。如果针对这个群体，通过健康生活方式引导、营养膳食改善和科学适当运动，则可以为“备老人群”健康老龄化更好地打下基础、延缓衰老和预防各种慢性病及老年病的过早发生，更有机会和更长时间地在身心愉悦中享受健康优雅慢慢老去的生活。

报告提到：面对复杂多变的持续老龄化带来的营养健康需求和挑战，推动科技创新和产业发展，突破技术瓶颈解决产品限制，加强适老食品研发和提升产品可及性等一系列措施成为必由之路。

报告建议，企业需要重点关注和解决咀嚼吞咽障碍、高蛋白、低GI等有专门针对性的产品研发、生产和推广，积极努力在备老阶段，就做好营养健康改善的精准性、可及性和可持续性，为即将到来的老年人群营养健康改善提供更坚实的科技基础。比如，液态奶具有合适的营养成分比例、适配老年生理特点的流体形态以及方便即饮的使用属性，成为老年群体营养支持体系的优选方案；当膳食摄入难以满足营养需求时，适当补充营养素具有积极意义，可遵循营养需求导向进行合理补充，如复合维生素矿物质片能系统性弥补因摄入不足和消化吸收功能下降导致的营养缺口。

此外，随着年龄增加，老年人群可能呈现更为复杂的疾病状况，结合老年人群疾病发生发展特点，进一步研发维护老年人群身体生理健康状态、全方位、均衡的全营养配方食品，满足老年病人群特定疾病状态下的营养需求的特定配方食品，以及满足不同老年人群营养需要的非全营养配方食品等。

研究显示：营养可以发挥具体的支持作用、甚至是治疗作用的方面包括：改善营养不良与肌肉衰减，促进认知功能与心理健康，提高免疫力与抗感染能力等重要作用。健康可以通过在日常生活中践行食物多样，合理搭配，适量摄入优质蛋白质，控制盐、油、糖的摄入，增加蔬果和全谷物摄入，保持适宜体重，规律进餐与适量饮水等方式实现。

中国营养学会秘书长韩军花表示：“我们以往的研究确实更多聚焦于65岁以上人群，但这次我们希望呼吁中年群体提前行动。从健康角度来看，中年阶段是预防老年疾病的关键时期。如果在这个阶段打好基础，未来可能对减少疾病发病率、延长寿命等方面都有积极影响。”

On May 26, 2025, Xinhua News reported on the release of the "Research Report on the Current Status and Improvement Strategies of Nutritional Health Issues in the Chinese Elderly Population," compiled by the Chinese Nutrition Society with support from Tetra Pak. The report was unveiled at the China Dairy Industry Association's 31st Annual Conference in Nanjing. It focuses on the "pre-aging population" (ages 45–64), emphasizing that nutritional supplementation should be planned early and scientifically intervened to improve health outcomes in old age.

Key findings include:
- **Definition of "pre-aging population":** People aged 45–64, who are still active but experiencing gradual physical decline.
- **Dietary issues:** Total energy intake slightly exceeds recommendations; fat intake exceeds 30% of total energy (men 33.7%, women 32.6%); over half have protein intake below recommended levels; vegetable and fruit intake is below guidelines; dairy (16.7–23.2g/day) and soy product intake are severely deficient.
- **Health risks:** High prevalence of diabetes (15–20% in 50–64 age group), obesity (peaking in men at 50–54), dyslipidemia, and cardiovascular disease risk.
- **Nutritional recommendations:** Improve dietary structure, increase high-quality protein, vegetables, fruits, and dairy; consider supplements like multivitamins and liquid milk; develop targeted foods for elderly needs (e.g., high-protein, low-GI, easy-to-chew products).
- **Expert quote:** Chinese Nutrition Society Secretary-General Han Junhua noted that previous research focused on those over 65, but this report calls for middle-aged groups to take proactive action to prevent diseases and extend healthy lifespan.

1. Fill ½ of your plate with vegetables and fruits (potatoes don't count due to blood sugar impact).
2. Fill ¼ with whole grains (whole wheat, barley, quinoa, oats, brown rice, etc.).
3. Fill ¼ with healthy protein (fish, chicken, beans, nuts; limit red meat, avoid processed meats).
4. Use healthy oils in moderation (olive, canola, soybean, corn, sunflower, peanut oils; avoid partially hydrogenated oils with trans fats).
5. Drink water, coffee, or tea; avoid sugary drinks; limit milk/dairy to 1-2 servings/day and juice to 1 small glass/day.
6. Stay active (symbolized by a red running figure under the plate).

The page emphasizes diet quality over quantity, noting that the type of carbohydrate matters more than the amount, and that healthy oils have no upper calorie limit. It also includes detailed usage terms for reproducing the Healthy Eating Plate image, requiring attribution, non-commercial use, no alterations, and compliance with Harvard's guidelines.

This webpage from The Spruce Eats provides a comprehensive guide to making congee (Chinese rice porridge), a classic breakfast dish also popular in Burma, Indonesia, Japan, and parts of Europe. Congee is made by boiling rice in a large amount of water until it reaches a pudding-like consistency. The article notes that 3/4 cup of rice yields 6 cups of porridge, making it economical and traditionally used to stretch rice when food is scarce. It is often served to children and those who are ill due to its easy digestibility.

The guide covers the best types of rice (white long-grain, jasmine, basmati, short-grain, or brown rice with longer cooking times), and offers three cooking methods:

**Method 2 (Oil method):** Soak rice, mix with 1 tsp oil, boil water, add rice, stir for 5 minutes, then simmer covered for 45 minutes. Oil helps the rice cook faster and results in smoother texture.

**Method 3 (Freezing method):** Soak rice, freeze for 2-3 hours, then add to boiling water and cook for 15 minutes, then let sit covered for 15 minutes. Freezing results in a smoother texture.

The recipe includes optional flavorings and toppings such as minced ginger, garlic, lotus root, gingko nuts, shredded chicken/pork, shredded bok choy, soft-boiled egg, and chopped peanuts. --- SOURCE 7: Trends in diet structural composition and quality among adults in Beijing, China (2010–2022) ---
URL: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12226269

SUMMARY:
<summary>
This study, published in Frontiers in Nutrition (June 2025), analyzed dietary trends among Beijing adults using three waves (2010, 2015, 2022) of data from the China Nutrition and Health Surveillance (CNHS), with 4,520 participants total. Dietary intake was assessed via 3-day 24-hour recalls plus household weighing of oils and condiments. Diet quality was evaluated using the Chinese Diet Balance Index (DBI-22).

**Key Findings:**
- **Macronutrient shifts (2010-2022):** Carbohydrate energy contribution decreased from 56.1% to 46.7% (below the recommended 50% minimum), while fat intake increased from 31.6% to 36.9% (exceeding the 30% upper limit), and protein increased from 12.0% to 14.9%.
- **Food source transition:** A shift from plant-based to animal-sourced foods occurred. Animal-based foods' contribution to energy rose from 13.4% to 23.9%, to protein from 29.2% to 48.0%, and to fat from 27.8% to 41.6% (all p<0.001).
- **Diet quality (DBI-22):** Persistent dietary imbalances were found—insufficient intake of vegetables, fruits, dairy, aquatic products, and soybeans (median scores: −1.5 to −6), and excessive intake of cereals, meat, eggs, oil, and salt (median scores: 1 to 4.7). Excess intake worsened over time (p=0.001), while intake deficiency modestly improved (p=0.004). The overall Diet Quality Distance (DQD) remained unchanged (p=0.868).
- **Subgroup differences:** Urban residents had better overall diet quality, while rural-urban disparities showed divergent trends. Women had better dietary quality than men. The 45-59 age group had the poorest diet quality.

**Conclusion:** Beijing adults experienced substantial dietary imbalances characterized by decreasing carbohydrate energy and increasing fat energy, both diverging from recommended levels. Dietary deficiencies and excesses coexist, contributing to suboptimal dietary quality.
</summary>

SUMMARY:
<summary>
This study, published in the International Journal of Public Health on January 13, 2023, examines differences in awareness of the 2016 Chinese Dietary Guidelines (CDGs) between urban and rural residents in Southwest China (Chongqing, Sichuan, Guizhou, and Yunnan). The cross-sectional survey included 8,320 participants aged 18-75, conducted between February and May 2021 using convenience sampling and face-to-face interviews.

**Key Findings:**
- Overall CDGs awareness was low: 29.1% in urban areas vs. 19.9% in rural areas (25.6% overall).
- Urban residents had higher correct answer rates on 10 of 12 knowledge questions.
- Factors influencing CDGs awareness included: region, education level, BMI, gender, income, and age.
- Higher education was a major predictor of awareness (OR: 2.07 for high vs. low education).
- Females had better awareness than males (OR: 1.24).
- In urban areas, middle-aged/elderly, higher-income, and obese individuals had better awareness; these associations were not significant in rural areas.
- Information channels differed: urban residents relied more on social media, books/magazines, family/friends, and experts; rural residents were more likely to get information from food sales staff.
- Social media was the most common source overall; food sales staff was the least common.

**Conclusions:** The study reveals a significant urban-rural gap in dietary knowledge in Southwest China. Future dietary education should adopt different strategies for different populations, with particular focus on rural residents, males, laborers, young people, less educated individuals, and those with low incomes. The findings provide a reference for promoting the latest edition of CDGs (2022).
</summary>

# Summary: Dietary Guidance for Hyperlipidemia (High Blood Fat) Patients

This webpage, published on the Nan'an City Government website on March 16, 2023, and sourced from "China Nutrition and Health," provides comprehensive dietary guidance for individuals with hyperlipidemia (high blood fat). It is based on the **"Dietary Guidance for Adult Hyperlipidemia (2023 Edition)"** issued by China's National Health Commission in January 2023.

## Key Content

### What is Hyperlipidemia?
Hyperlipidemia is a condition where one or more types of lipids (fats) in the blood exceed normal levels, including total cholesterol, LDL cholesterol, and triglycerides. Its prevalence has increased significantly in China over the past 30 years. It is a major risk factor for hypertension, diabetes, coronary heart disease, and stroke, and can lead to atherosclerosis.

### Eight Core Dietary Principles and Recommendations

1.  **Exercise & Weight Management:** Maintain a healthy weight through diet and exercise. Overweight/obese individuals should reduce daily energy intake by 300-500 kcal. Aim for 5-7 sessions of moderate-to-vigorous physical activity per week (30 min each), burning at least 200 kcal per session.

2.  **Fat Control & Low-Oil Cooking:**
    - Total fat: 20-25% of total energy intake.
    - Cooking oil: ≤ 25g per day.
    - Saturated fat: < 10% of total energy (< 7% for those with high cholesterol).
    - Dietary cholesterol: < 300mg/day (< 200mg for high cholesterol patients).
    - Trans fats: < 1% of total energy (≤ 2g/day).
    - Increase intake of unsaturated fats (e.g., n-3 polyunsaturated fatty acids).

3.  **Diverse Diet with Adequate Protein & Fiber:**
    - Limit refined grains; increase whole grains, legumes, and vegetables.
    - Daily fiber: 25-40g (including 7-13g soluble fiber).
    - Choose lean proteins: fish, skinless poultry, lean meat, low-fat/dairy, and soy protein.

4.  **Low Salt, Sugar Control, No Smoking, Limit Alcohol:**
    - Salt: ≤ 5g per day.
    - Limit added sugars and sweets.
    - Maintain regular作息, positive mood, adequate sleep, quit smoking, and limit alcohol.

5.  **Personalized Diet (TCM-Based):** Tailor plans based on age, gender, constitution, lifestyle, and TCM syndrome differentiation.

6.  **Seasonal Adjustments:** Adapt diet according to seasonal changes, as blood lipid levels can fluctuate.

7.  **Regional Adaptation:** Adjust diet based on local climate, dietary habits, and TCM constitution.

8.  **Scientific Eating:** Read nutrition labels; consume foods rich in plant sterols (about 2g/day) and polysaccharides; use food-medicine substances appropriately.

### Sample Meal Plan (3-Day Example for Phlegm-Turbidity Internal Obstruction Type)

The guide provides a 3-day sample menu for the TCM syndrome type "Phlegm-Turbidity Internal Obstruction" (痰浊内阻型), characterized by obesity, heaviness, drowsiness, fatigue, chest tightness, and sticky stools. The plan provides approximately 1790-1880 kcal, 80-90g protein, 245-275g carbohydrates, and 45-50g fat per day. Key features include:
- Use of therapeutic teas (e.g., Hawthorn-Chrysanthemum-Cassia Seed Tea, Three Fresh Tea).
- Use of functional soups (e.g., Winter Melon, Lotus Seedpod, and Coix Seed Lean Pork Soup).
- Recommended ingredients include whole grains, lean meats, fish, plenty of vegetables, and limited oil (20g) and salt (5g) per day.
- Foods with medicinal properties (e.g., hawthorn, chrysanthemum, cassia seed, tangerine peel, coix seed) are incorporated.
</summary>

SUMMARY:
<summary>
# 《中国高血压健康管理规范（2019）》摘要

该规范由国家心血管病中心、中国医学科学院阜外医院、中国疾病预防控制中心、中华医学会心血管病学分会等多家权威机构联合制定，发表于《中华心血管病杂志》2020年第48卷第1期。

## 核心内容概述

该规范强调高血压防线前移，面向全人群（健康人群、高血压易患人群和高血压患者），提供全方位的血压健康管理服务指导，内容包括健康信息收集、筛查评估、膳食指导、运动干预、心理疏导、药物治疗等。

## 高血压诊断标准
- 非同日3次测量收缩压≥140 mmHg和/或舒张压≥90 mmHg
- 24小时平均血压≥130/80 mmHg
- 连续监测5-7天平均血压≥135/85 mmHg

## 高血压易患人群危险因素
包括：高血压前期（收缩压120-139 mmHg和/或舒张压80-89 mmHg）、年龄≥45岁、超重和肥胖（BMI≥24 kg/m²）、家族史、高盐饮食、长期大量饮酒、吸烟、缺乏体力活动、长期精神紧张等。

## 生活方式干预要点

### 营养指导
- 每日食盐摄入量<5.0克（世界卫生组织推荐）
- 平衡膳食，食物多样化，每日摄入12种以上食物
- 控制总能量摄入，减少饱和脂肪酸和精制糖
- 限制饮酒：男性每日酒精<25g，女性<15g

### 运动指导
- 每周至少150分钟中等强度运动或75分钟较大强度运动
- 中等强度运动可使收缩压下降5-17 mmHg，舒张压下降2-10 mmHg
- 循序渐进，避免肌肉骨骼损伤

### 心理指导
- 焦虑使高血压患病风险增加约2倍，抑郁使女性患病风险增加约3.5倍
- 倡导"5125"健康生活理念（我要爱我）

## 高血压患者管理目标
- 单纯高血压患者：血压降至<140/90 mmHg，能耐受者可进一步降至<130/80 mmHg
- 合并糖尿病、慢性肾脏病、冠心病、心力衰竭、心房颤动患者：推荐降至<130/80 mmHg
- 采用综合干预策略，包括生活方式干预和药物治疗

## 儿童青少年高血压管理
- 3-17岁儿童青少年每年至少测量1次血压
- 肥胖儿童应控制体重，增加运动，平衡膳食
- 药物治疗适用于2级高血压、有临床症状或靶器官损害者

## 中医药应用
中医药治疗可配合降压药物使用，包括中药、针灸、推拿、刮痧、耳穴疗法、药浴、气功、太极拳等。

## 分级管理体系
建立由综合性医院、基层医疗卫生机构、疾病预防控制机构、健康管理机构组成的四级管理体系，实施双向转诊制度。

## 委员会组成
专家委员会主任委员为胡盛寿，副主任委员包括韩雅玲、蔡军、孙英贤、李玉明、张伟丽，编写委员会由全国70余位专家组成。
</summary>

<key_excerpts>
高血压是我国患病人数最多的慢性病之一，是城乡居民心脑血管疾病死亡的最重要的危险因素，但是高血压的知晓率、治疗率和控制率总体仍处于较低水平。,该规范是落实健康中国行动的重要举措，有助于促进高血压防控工作的规范化。,在未服用降压药物的情况下，非同日3次测量收缩压≥140 mmHg和/或舒张压≥90 mmHg，可诊断为高血压。,单纯高血压患者血压应降至<140/90 mmHg，能耐受者可进一步降至<130/80 mmHg。
</key_excerpts>

The guidelines address age-related physiological changes (declining metabolism, organ function, muscle mass, etc.) that affect nutrient absorption and increase disease risk, and provide core recommendations for two age groups:

**For General Elderly (65–79 years old):**
1. Eat a variety of foods, ensure adequate animal-based foods, and regularly consume soy products. Aim for 120–150g of animal protein daily (40–50g each of fish, meat, and eggs), 300–400ml of milk, and diverse fruits and vegetables.

3. Engage in outdoor activities to slow muscle loss and maintain a healthy weight (BMI 20–26.9 kg/m²).
4. Have regular health check-ups (1–2 times per year) and assess nutritional status to prevent deficiencies.

**For the Oldest-Old (80 years and above):**
1. Eat a diverse diet and encourage various ways of eating (e.g., shared meals, assisted feeding). Ensure at least 1 egg, 1 glass of milk, and 1–2 types of staples at breakfast; similar variety at lunch and dinner.
2. Choose soft, easily chewable and swallowable foods with high energy and nutrient density.
3. Eat sufficient fish, poultry, eggs, milk, and soy products daily (same serving sizes as above), plus vegetables and fruits.
4. Monitor weight loss and conduct regular nutritional screening to prevent malnutrition (target BMI 20–26.9 kg/m²).
5. Supplement with fortified foods or nutrient supplements under professional guidance when necessary.
6. Engage in physical activity (≥150 minutes per week) and cognitive activities (reading, games, etc.) to maintain physical and mental health.

**一、国民营养计划**：国务院和贵州省出台了《国民营养计划》及其实施方案，目标包括：降低5岁以下儿童和孕妇贫血率；5岁以下儿童生长迟缓率下降三分之一；0-6个月婴儿纯母乳喂养率提高10%；控制学生肥胖率；三级医院临床营养科建立覆盖率达到100%；居民营养健康知识知晓率达到95%；人均每日食盐摄入量控制在5克以下；居民超重肥胖增速控制在10%以内；保持消除碘缺乏危害状态。

**二、中国居民膳食指南（2022）核心要点**：
- 每日摄入12种以上食物，每周25种以上。
- 蔬菜水果不可互相替代；蔬菜维生素、矿物质和膳食纤维含量高于水果，水果碳水化合物和有机酸较多。

**三、营养素**：人体七大必需营养素包括蛋白质、碳水化合物、脂肪、矿物质、维生素、水、膳食纤维。能量主要来自碳水化合物、脂肪和蛋白质。粗粮富含膳食纤维但不宜过量，应粗细搭配。

**Background & Methods:** The CDGs were first released in 1989, with revisions in 1997 and 2007. The 2016 revision was conducted by an expert committee using the WHO Handbook for Guideline Development and the GRADE approach for evidence quality assessment. Evidence was drawn from Chinese journals (1997–2014) and English journals (2002–2014), along with national dietary surveys, Chinese DRIs (2013), and the Chinese Nutrition and Chronic Disease Report.

**Key Context:** China's dietary patterns shifted dramatically with economic growth. From 2007 to 2014, rural grain consumption dropped from 199.5 to 167.6 kg per capita, while meat and poultry consumption rose 56.1%. 1. Eat a variety of foods in a cereal-based diet (12 different foods daily, 25+ weekly; 250–400 g cereals/tubers/legumes including 50–150 g whole grains)

SUMMARY:

This webpage is a comprehensive guide for coaches on the Mifflin-St Jeor equation for estimating Basal Metabolic Rate (BMR). The formula is: BMR = (10 x weight in kg) + (6.25 x height in cm) - (5 x age in years), then add 5 for men or subtract 161 for women. It was published in 1990 and is considered the most accurate option for modern populations, with an average margin of error of ~5%, compared to 5-15% for the older Harris-Benedict formula (1919, revised 1984).

The guide provides three worked client profiles (sedentary office worker, moderately active sales rep, very active triathlete) showing the full calculation from BMR to TDEE using activity multipliers ranging from 1.2 (sedentary) to 1.9 (extremely active). A key insight is that the activity multiplier makes more difference than the formula itself.

Key limitations: The equation doesn't work well for very muscular clients (Katch-McArdle is better), obese clients with BMI over 35 (overestimates BMR by 5-10%), and adults over 65 (additional 5-10% reduction needed). The guide recommends recalculating BMR every 4-6 weeks or whenever a client gains/loses more than 3 kg. The most common mistake is overestimating activity level. The page also promotes Promealplan as a tool that automates these calculations and generates meal plans.
</summary>

<summary>
The webpage is dedicated to the Mifflin–St Jeor equation, the most validated BMR (Basal Metabolic Rate) formula for healthy adults, published in 1990. It is the default formula used by modern TDEE calculators, including the one on this site.

**The Formula:**
- Men: BMR = (10 × weight in kg) + (6.25 × height in cm) - (5 × age in years) + 5
- Women: BMR = (10 × weight in kg) + (6.25 × height in cm) - (5 × age in years) - 161

**How to Use for Daily Calories:**

2. Multiply by an activity multiplier (1.2 to 1.9).
3. Subtract 250–500 kcal for fat loss or add 250–500 kcal for muscle gain.
4. Round to the nearest 50 kcal.

**Key BMR Equations:**

--- SOURCE 1: Protein Requirements for Older Adults - The Geriatric Dietitian ---
URL: https://thegeriatricdietitian.com/protein-requirements-for-older-adults

SUMMARY:
<summary>
This article from The Geriatric Dietitian discusses protein requirements for older adults, emphasizing that while the Dietary Reference Intake (DRI) for adults is 0.8 grams of protein per kilogram of body weight, emerging research suggests older adults need more. The PROT-AGE Study Group (2013) and the European Society for Clinical Nutrition and Metabolism (ESPEN) recommend that older adults consume 1-1.2 grams of protein per kilogram body weight to preserve muscle mass and support overall health. For a 150-pound individual, this translates to approximately 68-82 grams of protein daily, compared to 55 grams under the standard DRI.

Protein is essential for preventing sarcopenia (gradual muscle loss with aging), supporting immunity, and maintaining physical function. The article recommends spreading protein intake throughout the day (about 30 grams per meal) for optimal muscle protein synthesis, prioritizing whole food sources like meat, eggs, and dairy, and using protein supplements (powders or drinks) only when dietary interventions fail. Caution is advised against excessive protein intake, particularly for individuals with kidney disease, and exercise (resistance and endurance) should be combined with adequate protein to protect muscle mass.
</summary>

--- SOURCE 2: Protein Needs for Adults 50+ | Lifestyle Medicine ---
URL: https://lifestylemedicine.stanford.edu/protein-needs-for-adults-50

SUMMARY:
<summary>
This Stanford Lifestyle Medicine article discusses protein needs for adults aged 50 and older, authored by Sharon Brock with expert input from Marily Oppezzo, PhD, MS, RDN, DipACLM.

**Key Recommendations:**
- For adults 50+, consume 1.2–1.6 grams of protein per kg of body weight daily (0.54–0.72 grams/pound). For a 165-pound adult, this equals roughly 90–120 grams per day.
- To build muscle past age 50, adequate protein intake must be combined with weight training, consuming 30–35 grams of protein within two hours of the workout.
- Due to anabolic resistance (reduced muscle protein synthesis response to protein) that increases with age, it's recommended to increase protein per meal to roughly 30–35 grams (0.4 g/kg per meal).

**Why More Protein is Needed with Age:**
- Starting around age 30, muscle mass declines 1–2% per year, with the rate increasing to 3–10% per decade after 60.
- A study comparing men aged ~22 vs ~71 found that older men needed 40 grams of protein per meal to stimulate muscle synthesis, while younger men responded equally well to 20 or 40 grams.
- The body prioritizes protein for other functions (brain, liver, immune system) over muscle maintenance, requiring higher intake specifically for muscle preservation.

**Best Protein Sources:**
- Whole food sources are preferred over powders. If supplementing, whey protein or pea protein (vegan) are recommended.
- Leucine is the most important amino acid for muscle building, found in high quantities in whey and milk.

The federal guideline of 0.8 g/kg/day is considered too low for those over 50 by many experts. The article emphasizes that protein alone is insufficient—strength training is the most important way to prevent age-related muscle loss.
</summary>

Key recommendations include:
- **Optimal intake:** 0.45-0.7g per pound of body weight (vs. the RDA of 0.36g/lb), with the PROT-AGE Study Group and ESPEN recommending 1.0-1.6g/kg per day depending on activity level.
- **Per-meal doses:** Due to anabolic resistance, older adults need 30-40g of protein per meal (vs. 20g for younger adults) to trigger muscle protein synthesis.
- **Leucine threshold:** Older adults need 2.5-3g of leucine per meal. Top leucine sources include whey protein (2.7g/scoop), chicken breast (2.5g/4oz), and cottage cheese (2.4g/cup).
- **Distribution matters:** Evenly spreading protein across meals (especially breakfast, which should contain 25-40g) is more effective than concentrating it at dinner.
- **Exercise combination:** Resistance training (2-3 sessions/week) combined with adequate protein intake produces the best results for muscle maintenance and even regrowth in older adults.

The guide includes a sample meal plan (~130g protein for a 170lb 65-year-old), practical solutions for common barriers (reduced appetite, dental issues, cost, digestive problems), and addresses FAQs about kidney health, supplements, and the possibility of regaining muscle in later years.
</summary>

Older adults need more protein than younger adults, not less, Anabolic resistance means muscles need higher protein doses per meal (30-40g), Sarcopenia (age-related muscle loss) starts around age 30 and accelerates after 60, The PROT-AGE Study Group and ESPEN both recommend that healthy older adults consume at least 1.0-1.2 grams per kilogram (0.45-0.55 grams per pound) of body weight per day, Studies show that older adults who consume at least 25-40 grams of protein at breakfast maintain significantly more muscle mass than those who concentrate their intake at dinner

--- SOURCE 4: How Much Protein Do Adults Over 50 Need? ---
URL: https://www.eatingwell.com/how-much-protein-do-adults-over-50-need-11973826

SUMMARY:
<summary>
This article from EatingWell explains that adults over 50 may need more protein than the standard recommendation. While the RDA is 0.8 grams per kilogram of body weight, many experts recommend 1 to 1.2 g/kg/day for older adults. For a 150-pound person, this translates to roughly 68 to 82 grams of protein daily.

The increased need is due to age-related muscle loss (sarcopenia), with muscle mass declining 0.3% to 0.8% per year after age 30, and muscle strength deteriorating 2% to 4% annually after age 50–60. The body also becomes less efficient at using protein with age (anabolic resistance), requiring more protein to achieve the same effects.

Dietitians recommend spreading protein intake throughout the day, including it at all meals and snacks. Tips include starting with a protein-rich breakfast, adding legumes to dishes, and sprinkling seeds, nuts, cheese, or nutritional yeast on meals. Individual needs may vary based on illness, activity level, medical conditions, hormonal changes (e.g., menopause), and overall health.
</summary>

"Protein is essential for nearly every function in the body," says Lauren Manaker, M.S., RDN, LD., "This is because aging is associated with a natural decline in muscle mass, known as sarcopenia, which increases the need for dietary protein to maintain muscle health," explains Lauren Manaker., "As you age, the body becomes less efficient at using protein, meaning that older adults need a bit more protein to achieve the same effects as younger individuals," says Lisa Young, Ph.D., RDN., "Both bones and muscles become catabolic (or break down) at a slow rate as you age," explains Toby Amidor, M.S., RD.

URL: https://www.ncoa.org/article/how-much-protein-do-older-adults-need

SUMMARY:
<summary>
This article from the National Council on Aging (NCOA) explains the importance of protein intake for older adults and provides practical guidance on how much protein they need and how to get it.

- Adults age 19+ should aim for 0.8 grams of protein per kilogram of body weight daily (g/kg/day).
- Adults age 65+ should aim for about 1.0 to 1.2 g/kg/day.
- For a 160-pound older adult, this translates to about 80 grams of protein per day.
- Higher amounts are needed for recovering from surgery (1.6–3.0 g/kg/day) or active lifestyles (up to 1.7 g/kg/day).

**Why Protein Matters:** Protein helps slow age-related muscle loss (sarcopenia), supports immune function, aids recovery from illness/injury, and reduces frailty risk. About 1 in 3 people over 50 fall short of daily protein requirements.

**Practical Tips:**
- Eat protein first at meals, use Greek yogurt, snack on high-protein foods, try plant-based sources (beans, lentils, tofu, quinoa), add protein boosts (milk powder, almonds, cottage cheese), and consider oral nutrition supplements if appetite is poor.
- Space protein intake evenly throughout the day (20-30g per meal, 10-20g per snack) rather than consuming most at dinner.
- Track intake for a few days using general serving guidelines (e.g., 3 oz meat = 22-28g protein, 6 oz Greek yogurt = 18g, 1 egg = 12.4g).

The article includes a caution for those with kidney disease to consult a doctor before changing protein intake, and recommends using tools like MyPlate.gov or protein calculators for personalized guidance.

SUMMARY:

This is a systematic review and meta-analysis published in Nutrients (2024) examining the association between protein intake and sarcopenia among Korean older adults (aged 65+). Researchers analyzed 23 studies (16 cross-sectional, 5 RCTs, 2 non-RCTs) with 9 included in the meta-analysis.

URL: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC2760315

SUMMARY:
<summary>
This article by Paddon-Jones and Rasmussen (2009), published in Current Opinion in Clinical Nutrition and Metabolic Care, reviews the role of dietary protein in preventing sarcopenia (age-related muscle loss). Key findings: 

- Sarcopenia is characterized by a 3-8% reduction in lean muscle mass per decade after age 30, affecting 30% of those over 60 and more than 50% of those over 80.
- Ageing does not inevitably reduce the anabolic response to high-quality protein; ingestion of 25-30g of protein per meal maximally stimulates muscle protein synthesis in both young and older individuals.
- However, muscle protein synthesis is blunted in elderly when protein and carbohydrate are coingested or when protein quantity is less than ~20g per meal.
- The current RDA for protein (0.8g/kg/day for all adults 19+) was based on short-duration nitrogen balance studies in young adults and may not be optimal for preventing sarcopenic muscle loss.
- Supplementing meals with leucine (a potent activator of the mTOR signaling pathway) may enhance muscle protein synthesis in ageing muscle.
- Physical activity (even moderate walking) can sensitize ageing muscle to nutritional stimuli and help restore normal protein anabolic responses.
- The authors propose a practical dietary plan: 25-30g of high-quality protein per meal, distributed evenly across meals, rather than a large global increase in total daily protein intake.
</summary>

--- SOURCE 1: 宏量营养素 ---
URL: https://baike.baidu.com/item/%E5%AE%8F%E9%87%8F%E8%90%A5%E5%85%BB%E7%B4%A0/11053686

SUMMARY:
<summary>
宏量营养素（又称能量营养素）是指人体需要量较大的三类主要营养物质：蛋白质、脂类和碳水化合物。它们是人体主要的能量来源，也参与构成细胞和组织、维持生命活动等生理功能。成年人每日约70%的能量来源于这三类物质。

根据《中国居民膳食营养素参考摄入量（2023版）》，建议成年人膳食中碳水化合物供能占50%-65%，脂肪占20%-30%，蛋白质占10%-20%（65岁以上老年人蛋白质供能比应达到15%）。每克碳水化合物和蛋白质分别提供4千卡能量，每克脂肪提供9千卡能量。

发展历程方面，19世纪上半叶科学家们发现并命名了蛋白质、脂类和碳水化合物；19世纪末Atwater等人确定了三大营养素的可代谢能量值；1994年确立了膳食营养素参考摄入量；2013年中国营养学会首次修订了中国居民膳食营养素参考摄入量；2023年发布了新版标准。

宏量营养素的生理功能包括：碳水化合物是脑组织唯一能量来源，脂肪储存能量效率最高（占人体总储备85%以上），蛋白质在能量不足时参与供能。此外，蛋白质构成肌肉、酶和抗体，磷脂是细胞膜基本成分，脂肪组织分泌瘦素调控食欲等。

应用方面，不同人群需求不同。运动中可每小时补充30-60g易吸收碳水，运动后按碳水与蛋白质3:1比例补充；耐力运动员碳水化合物摄入需提升至8-10g/kg/日，力量型运动员蛋白质上限可达2.5g/kg/日。

影响方面，摄入不均衡可能导致必需营养素缺乏或增加慢性病风险。碳水化合物供能比低于40%或高于70%均可能增加死亡率；脂肪摄入超过推荐上限会增加肥胖、心血管疾病风险。中国居民膳食结构正从高碳水化合物模式向高脂肪模式转变，1982年至2012年脂肪供能比从18.4%增至32.9%，已超过推荐上限。

相关研究指出，单纯控制宏量营养素比例而非总能量无法有效控制体重，低碳水饮食在预防疾病方面的长期健康效应证据尚不充分。
</summary>

<key_excerpts>
宏量营养素，又称能量营养素，是指人体需要量较大的三类主要营养物质，包括蛋白质、脂类和碳水化合物。它们是人体主要的能量来源，也参与构成细胞和组织、维持生命活动等生理功能。成年人每日约70%的能量来源于这三类物质。建议成年人膳食中碳水化合物供能占50%-65%，脂肪占20%-30%，蛋白质占10%-20%。每克碳水化合物、蛋白质、脂肪分别提供4、4、9千卡能量。中国居民膳食中脂肪的供能比已从1982年的18.4%增加到2012年的32.9%，超过了推荐上限。单纯控制宏量营养素比例而非总能量无法有效控制体重。
</key_excerpts>

SUMMARY:
<summary>
This webpage provides dietary intake guidelines for the three macronutrients (carbohydrates, protein, and fat) based on the **Chinese Dietary Guidelines (2022)**. It specifies the recommended proportion of total daily energy intake for each macronutrient for adults:

- **Carbohydrates**: 50–65% of daily energy (about 250–300g), with a preference for whole grains over refined grains.
- **Protein**: 10–15% of daily energy (about 55–65g). Animal protein is more bioavailable than plant protein; both types should be consumed together for complementary benefits.
- **Fat**: 20–30% of daily energy (with cooking oil <5g). Prioritize unsaturated fatty acids (especially essential fatty acids like linoleic acid at ~4%E or 12g, and α-linolenic acid at ~0.6%E or 2g), limit saturated fat (<8%E), and avoid trans fats.

The page emphasizes that carbohydrates are the sole energy source for the brain and nervous system, proteins are essential for immune function and tissue repair, and fats are crucial for energy storage and organ protection.

《中国居民膳食指南（2022）》其准则一‘食物多样，合理搭配’，明确指出三大宏量营养素在成年人每日膳食总能量所占的比例，分别为：碳水化合物50~65%，蛋白质10~15%，脂肪20~30%。, 糖类（碳水化合物）也是大脑和神经系统所需能量的唯一来源。, 动物蛋白的蛋白质种类和结构更接近人体的蛋白结构和数量，人体更容易吸收利用，且一般都含有人类所必需的9种氨基酸（特别奶制品和蛋类），完整性更高。

--- SOURCE 3: 中国9省(区)2000－2011年成年女性膳食营养素摄入变化趋势 ---
URL: https://html.rhhz.net/zhlxbx/20150711.htm

SUMMARY:
<summary>
This study, published in the *Chinese Journal of Epidemiology* (2015), analyzes trends in dietary nutrient intake among adult females (ages 25–55) in nine Chinese provinces from 2000 to 2011, using data from the China Health and Nutrition Survey (CHNS) and comparing against the 2013 Chinese Dietary Reference Intakes (DRIs). Key findings include:

- **Energy & Macronutrients:** The proportion of women meeting energy and protein recommendations declined. In 2011, only 43.0% met energy requirements and 54.4% met protein requirements. Carbohydrate intake decreased (40.2% had low carbohydrate intake <50% energy), while fat intake increased substantially (63.8% had high fat intake >30% energy). Rural women saw a dramatic rise in high fat intake (from 38.6% in 2000 to 59.7% in 2011), while urban women reached 73.1% in 2011.
- **Vitamins:** Vitamin intake was poor except for vitamin E (88.5% met recommendation in 2011). Vitamin A adequacy was 25.2%, thiamine 10.7%, riboflavin 6.9%, niacin 54.9%, and vitamin C 24.3%. Most showed declining trends.
- **Minerals:** Calcium intake was critically low—only 3.3% met recommendations. Magnesium adequacy was 23.6%, selenium 13.3%, iron 50.9%, and zinc 75.7%. Most showed declining trends.
- **Other trends:** Overweight/obesity rates increased from 35.9% (2000) to 41.1% (2011). The sample included 14,515 women across five survey rounds. The study attributes these trends to dietary shifts toward higher fat, lower carbohydrate, and lower micronutrient intake, driven by urbanization, increased eating out, and changing food consumption patterns.

**Conclusion:** The dietary nutritional status of adult women in these provinces requires improvement. Targeted nutrition education and interventions are recommended.

SUMMARY:
<summary>
This webpage is a chapter from an open-access nutrition science textbook (LibreTexts) titled "4.2: Defining Nutrient Requirements- Dietary Reference Intakes." It explains the Dietary Reference Intakes (DRIs), a set of nutrient and energy intake recommendations developed by the National Academies of Sciences, Engineering, Medicine for healthy individuals in the U.S. and Canada.

The DRIs are divided into two categories: energy intake recommendations and nutrient intake recommendations.

**Energy Intake Recommendations:**
- **Estimated Energy Requirement (EER):** Average daily calorie intake needed to maintain energy balance based on age, sex, height, weight, and physical activity level.
- **Acceptable Macronutrient Distribution Ranges (AMDRs):** Recommended percentage ranges of daily calories from carbohydrates (45-65%), fat (20-35%), and protein (10-35%).

**Nutrient Intake Recommendations (four DRI values):**
1. **Estimated Average Requirement (EAR):** Amount meeting the needs of 50% of healthy individuals in a given life stage/sex group.
2. **Recommended Dietary Allowance (RDA):** Amount sufficient to meet the needs of 97-98% of the healthy population (derived from EAR).
3. **Adequate Intake (AI):** Used when insufficient evidence exists for an RDA; based on observed intakes of healthy people.
4. **Tolerable Upper Intake Level (UL):** The highest daily intake likely to pose no risk of adverse effects; exceeding it increases toxicity risk.

The page notes that the RDA is a recommendation, not an individual requirement, and that there is typically a wide safety margin between RDA and UL. The DRIs are used by health professionals, for dietary guidelines (e.g., MyPlate, Dietary Guidelines for Americans), nutrition labeling, assistance programs (school meals, WIC, SNAP), nutrition monitoring, military meal planning, and the food/supplement industry.
</summary>

--- SOURCE 9: Description of the Acceptable Macronutrient Distribution Range - Rethinking the Acceptable Macronutrient Distribution Range for the 21st Century - NCBI Bookshelf ---
URL: https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK610333

SUMMARY:
<summary>
This webpage from the NCBI Bookshelf provides a chapter from the National Academies of Sciences, Engineering, and Medicine's 2024 letter report titled "Rethinking the Acceptable Macronutrient Distribution Range for the 21st Century." The chapter describes the development and application of the Acceptable Macronutrient Distribution Range (AMDR).

**Development of the Dietary Reference Intakes (DRIs):**
- In 1993, the Food and Nutrition Board held a symposium to explore revising the RDAs, aiming to unite concepts of a healthful diet with essential nutrient requirements.
- Under the old RDA paradigm, carbohydrate had no absolute dietary requirement, and fat was recommended at no more than 30% of dietary energy.
- Beginning in 1995, the DRI paradigm was established, introducing EARs, RDAs, and ULs. EARs and RDAs were set for carbohydrate (based on brain glucose use) and protein (based on nitrogen balance studies), but not for fat, SFAs, MUFAs, or cholesterol.

**Introduction of the AMDR:**
- The AMDR was proposed to provide intake guidance for energy-source macronutrients (carbohydrate, fat, omega-6 and omega-3 PUFAs, and protein) based on their role in chronic disease and the need for essential nutrients.
- AMDR values are presented as a percentage of total energy intake by age group, independent of sex.
- Intakes above the AMDR increase risk of chronic disease; intakes outside the range increase risk of nutrient insufficiency.
- Evidence base included intervention trials and observational data on chronic disease prevention and micronutrient adequacy.

**Application of the AMDRs:**
- For individuals: diets should be designed so macronutrient intakes fall within their AMDRs while meeting RDA/AI and remaining below UL.
- For groups: one method is to develop menus with mean intakes at the midpoint of each AMDR; another is to plan dietary patterns with mean fat intake at 30% of total energy.
- The AMDR is intended as a general quantitative guideline, with qualitative considerations (e.g., low saturated fat) remaining important.
- When assessing individuals, mean intakes between the lower and upper AMDR bounds may be acceptable; intakes below or above may indicate concerns.

**Summary:** The AMDR was established to guide health professionals on using a range of intakes for energy-containing macronutrients associated with both micronutrient adequacy and decreased chronic disease risk, based on the percent of total calories.
</summary>

For these nutrients, recommended intakes were presented as a percentage of total energy intake by age group.", "The supposition was that intakes above the AMDR increase the risk of chronic disease while intakes outside the range increase the risk of nutrient insufficiency.", "The AMDR was established to provide health professionals with guidance on using a range of intakes for energy-containing macronutrients (i.e., carbohydrate, protein, and fat) associated with both micronutrient intake adequacy and decreased risk of chronic disease."
</key_excerpts>

**Carbohydrates (45–65% of daily calories):** Primary energy source for the brain and body. Simple carbs (candy, fruit, sports drinks) provide quick energy, best for before/during activity. Complex carbs (whole grains, beans, starchy vegetables) provide sustained energy, better for everyday eating.

**Proteins (10–35% of daily calories):** Made of amino acids; essential for building bones, muscles, skin, and blood. Animal-based and soy proteins have higher amounts of essential amino acids. Choose lean protein sources (fewer legs = leaner). Aim for ¼ of your plate at each meal.

Unsaturated fats (vegetable oils, nuts, avocados, fish) support cell health and reduce inflammation. A small serving (1–2 tablespoons) of unsaturated fat per meal is sufficient.

The article recommends using the Power Plate tool to estimate individual needs and suggests focusing on one macronutrient at a time to build understanding.
